deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X and X̌ are dual real projective planes. T is a 'triangle' in X, meaning three lines 1, 2, 3 in general position, together with a choice of one of the four triangular cells they cut out (the hatched cell in the drawing). T' is the dual triangle in X̌: three points 1*, 2*, 3* and the three lines joining them, again with a chosen cell. Under duality, the vertex i∩j of T corresponds to the side of T' through i* and j*, and each side of T corresponds to a vertex of T'.

The point being recorded is an orientation bookkeeping under duality. Duality exchanges two kinds of orientation:
- An orientation of a line D in X is an orientation of the dual pencil. It therefore gives a local orientation (a sense of rotation) of X̌ at the point D*.
- A local orientation of X at a point p (a rotation sense of the pencil of lines through p) is an orientation of the dual line p*.

On the triangle side, take a vertex, say 2 = 1∩3, with the chosen cell attached to it. There is an orientation α of line 1, an orientation β of the other side through the vertex, and a local orientation ω of X at the vertex (the curled arrows; the cell is used to fix the choices). These are tied by ω = α∧β; the page calls them 'associées', i.e. coherent.

On the dual side, transport these by duality:
- α' is the local orientation of X̌ at the point 1*;
- β' is the local orientation at the other dual point;
- ω' is the orientation of the dual line joining them.

Grothendieck's observation is that the transported triple (α', β', ω') is NOT coherent in the same sense. This matches the previous page, where he writes ω = α∧β but ω* = −α*∧β*. So the correspondence between the orientation data of T and of T' carries a sign; it is not the naive 'associated' one. From this one gets corresponding orientations of the sides of T and T', and of X (resp. X̌) at the vertices of T (resp. T'). Hence, for a vertex of T in X and the corresponding side of T' in X̌ (and vice versa), the orientations correspond.

The lower drawings appear to illustrate the elementary move on triangles:
- Left: two crossing (orange) lines with a third line (dashed, in several positions) sweeping across the crossing point, with frames α, β, γ. This is a triangle flip / mutation.
- Bottom right: the dual picture, a point crossing the segment between two points, with frames α', β', γ'.

The page also records how the frames transform under this move. Purpose within the dossier: setting up the sign conventions needed to make projective duality of pseudoline systems compatible with orientations and with the group of symmetries σ0, σ1, σ2, ρs, ρf of a flagged triangle (vertex, side, cell) studied on the previous page.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the sign discrepancy (ω = α∧β versus ω' = −α'∧β' after dualizing) is the content being recorded rather than a mistake.

The phrase rendered 'non associée' in the first paragraph is hard to read. The intended statement is probably that the correspondence of orientations is not the naive/coherent one; the exact wording is uncertain.

ideas.what: Duality between the real projective plane and its dual exchanges orientations of lines with local orientations (rotation senses) of the plane at the dual points, and vice versa.
ideas.modern_name: Projective duality of local orientations / pencils; orientation conventions in dualizing (pseudo)line arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (projective geometry); for pseudoline arrangements, duality via Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ca. 1980–84)

ideas.what: Sign rule: a coherent frame (α, β, ω = α∧β) at a vertex of a triangle dualizes to a frame with ω' = −α'∧β', so orientation data of T and T' correspond only up to a definite sign.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation reversal under duality (sign conventions for chirotopes / oriented matroid duality of rank-3 configurations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in oriented matroid theory (Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence, 1978); no single attribution

ideas.what: Drawings of a line sweeping across a crossing and its dual (a point crossing a segment), with transported frames.
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation of pseudoline arrangements and its dual
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956); later Goodman–Pollack, Björner et al. 'Oriented Matroids'

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but standard sign bookkeeping for projective duality applied to flagged triangles, in service of Grothendieck's private theory of pseudoline systems. It is consistent with, and subsumed by, oriented matroid duality and the Goodman–Pollack duality of arrangements. There is nothing here a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The phrase transcribed 'non associée' (first paragraph) is uncertain in the image; it seems to say the correspondence of orientations is not the naive/associated one, and it may read differently.
'd'un pair de T et de T'' is probably 'des côtés de T et de T'' or similar; illegible as written.
The final line likely reads 'α, β, ω associés, mais α', β', ω' non associés', with 'non' underlined. Compare the previous page, which has 'orientés' / 'non orientés' and ω = α∧β, ω* = −α*∧β*.

The diagram description should note that the bottom figures show a line moving across a crossing point and, dually, a point crossing a segment between two points (frames α, β, γ and α', β', γ'), not merely 'two orange lines'.
